questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Syamala is __more taller__ than her sister.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Taller**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, "Syamala is more taller__ than her sister," the correct option is "**taller**."
 
• The reason for this is that the word "**taller**" already conveys the comparative degree, so adding "**more**" before it is redundant and grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct comparative form of the adjective "**tall**" is "**taller**."
 
• When comparing two things, people, or objects, we use the comparative form to indicate that one has a greater degree of the quality expressed by the adjective than the other.
 
• Therefore, the sentence should be: "*Syamala is taller than her sister.*"

Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Tall**: The positive form "tall" when not comparing two or more things, and simply want to describe the height of a single person or object. 
 
• **Most Taller**: This is incorrect in standard English. The correct form is "taller," not "most taller."
 
• **Tallest**: The superlative form "tallest" is used when comparing more than two things or people, and indicates that one has the greatest degree of height among them.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Hurray! Here is the toy / what I was looking for / as my birthday gift.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **what I was looking for.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The use of "**what**" instead of "**that**" is incorrect as "**what**" is used to ask for information and not to refer to a specific object.
 
• "**What**" is often used in non-restrictive relative clauses or in indirect questions.
 
 
• **For example**, "I got what I wanted." In this case, "what I wanted" is not essential to understanding the main clause.
 
 
 
• "**That**" is used to introduce restrictive relative clauses, providing essential information to identify or define the noun it modifies.
 
• The use of "**as**" is correct as it shows the reason for the gift.
 
• The correct relative pronoun to use in this case is "that**" **when referring to a specific thing.
 
• The **correct sentence** should be "*Hurray! Here is the toy that I was looking for as my birthday gift.*"

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Through these experiences, Sarah gained a newfound appreciation for the beauty and complexity of the world, and returned home with a renewed sense of purpose and passion.

B. Sarah had always dreamed of traveling the world, but she never had the opportunity to do so until she graduated from college.

C. Along the way, she encountered a diverse array of individuals, each with their own unique stories and perspectives.

D. With her degree in hand, she set off on a backpacking adventure across Europe, eager to explore new cultures and meet new people.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **BDCA**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Sentence **B**: This sentence introduces Sarah's dream of travelling and the circumstances that led her to fulfill that dream after graduating from college.
 
• Sentence **D**: This sentence follows up on the previous one by explaining how Sarah, after graduating from college, embarked on a backpacking adventure across Europe to fulfill her dream of travelling.
 
• Sentence **C**: This sentence provides details about Sarah's experiences during her travels, emphasizing the diversity of people she met and the different perspectives she encountered.
 
• Sentence **A**: The final sentence concludes the paragraph by highlighting the positive impact of Sarah's travels. It states that through these experiences, she gained appreciation and returned home with a renewed sense of purpose and passion.
 
• The paragraph follows a logical and chronological order, starting with Sarah's dream, her decision to travel after college, her experiences during the journey, and the positive impact it had on her.

So, the correct answer is **option 4**. ​

questions.question:
**Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

(A) to simplify filling taxes

(B) to a single flat rate

(C) the current five rates

(D) by narrowing

(E) Forbes wanted
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **EADCB**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **E**: This is the introductory part that sets the context for what Forbes desired or aimed for.
 
• **A**: This part follows the introduction and provides information about Forbes's objective, which is to simplify the process of filling taxes.
 
• **D**: This part explains the method or approach Forbes wanted to adopt to achieve their objective. They wanted to simplify the process by narrowing.
 
• **C**: This part adds more specificity to what Forbes wanted to narrow down; in this case, it's the current five tax rates.
 
• **B**: The final part concludes the sentence by specifying the desired outcome of Forbes's objective. They wanted to simplify the process by narrowing down the current five tax rates to a single flat rate.
 
• So, the sequence **EADCB **creates a coherent and meaningful sentence, starting with the introduction of Forbes's desire, followed by the objective, method, specifics, and the desired outcome.

Thus, **option 4** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

She killed the cockroach.

options.text: The cockroach was being killed by her.
The cockroach is killed by her.
The cockroach was killed by her.
The cockroach has been killed by her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**The cockroach was killed by her.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice in English is formed by using the auxiliary verb "**to be" + past participle of the main verb**.
 
• **Active voice structure**: Subject + Verb + Object__
 
• **Passive voice structure**: __Object of the Active + "to be" verb + Past Participle of the Main Verb + by + Subject of the Active Voice__
 
• In this sentence, "**killed**" is the past participle of the main verb "**to kill**".
 
• The subject of the sentence, "**she**", becomes the agent of the action in the passive voice sentence.
 
• Therefore, "**the cockroach**" becomes the subject of the sentence in the passive voice and is preceded by the auxiliary verb "**was**".

Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

A question asked by the student to the teacher during class.
A question will be asked by the student to the teacher during class.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**A question was asked by the student to the teacher during class.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Active voice structure**: Subject + Verb + Object__
 
• **Passive Voice structure**: __Object of the Active + "to be" verb + Past Participle of the Main Verb + by + Subject of the Active Voice__
 
• The sentence is in active voice, with the subject (**student**) performing the action (**asking the question**) on the object (**teacher**).
 
• To convert it to passive voice, we need to make the object (**a question**) the subject of the sentence, and the subject (**student**) will become the object of the preposition "**by**".
 
• The verb "**asked**" will become "**was asked**", and the preposition "**to**" will become "**by**".
 
• The phrase "**during class**" can remain at the end of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.
